```{python}
# Import necessary libraries
import pyspark as spark
import pyspark.sql.functions as sf
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from lets_plot import *
import plotly.express as px
import polars as pl

spark = SparkSession.builder.getOrCreate()


# Load in necessary tables
shoppers0 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/shoppers_0.parquet")
shoppers1 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/shoppers_1.parquet")
shoppers2 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/shoppers_2.parquet")
stores = spark.read.parquet("../Data/cstore_stores.parquet")
sets0 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/sets_0.parquet")
sets1 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/sets_1.parquet")
items0 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00000.parquet")
items1 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00001.parquet")
items2 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00002.parquet")
items3 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00003.parquet")
items4 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00004.parquet")
items5 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00005.parquet")
items6 = spark.read.parquet("../Data/part-00006.parquet")

# Create baseline tables

# Merge items tables
items = (
    items0
    .unionByName(items1)
    .unionByName(items2)
    .unionByName(items3)
    .unionByName(items4)
    .unionByName(items5)
    .unionByName(items6)
)

# Merge sets tables
sets = sets0.unionByName(sets1)

# Merge shoppers tables
shoppers = (
    shoppers0
    .unionByName(shoppers1)
    .unionByName(shoppers2)
)

# Change data type of Store ID in stores table
stores = stores.withColumn(
    "STORE_ID",
    sf.col("STORE_ID").cast("string")
)

# Join shoppers, transactions, items, and stores tables
joined_items = (shoppers
                .join(sets, on = "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", how = "left")
                .join(stores, "STORE_ID", how = "left")
                .withColumn("MONTH", sf.month("DATE_TIME"))
                .withColumn("YEAR", sf.year("DATE_TIME"))
                .join(items, "GTIN", how = "left"))

# Join shoppers, sets, and stores table. Create columns for year, month, and hour of each transaction set
joined_sets = (shoppers
               .join(sets, on = "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", how = "left")
               .join(stores, on = "STORE_ID", how = "left")
               .withColumn("MONTH", sf.month("DATE_TIME"))
               .withColumn("YEAR", sf.year("DATE_TIME"))
               .withColumn("TIME", sf.hour("DATE_TIME")))
```

I took convenience store sales data and created a couple of features that would be used by a clustering model to segment a convenience store's customer base. Data came from Dewey Data. I used PySpark to perform all the engineering. 

The first feature is the number of cycles it has been since the customer last shop. A cycle is the average number of days between visits.
